To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
human alpha 1-adrenergic receptors have been cloned and characterized.

we have cloned and characterized human alpha 1A, alpha 1B, and alpha 1C adrenergic (ADRENERGIC RECEPTORS) receptor subtypes, that we have made sequence corrections to previously published data, and that we have compared human alpha 1ADRENERGICS with other species homologue subtypes.
human alpha 1A and alpha 1D adrenergic (AR) receptor cDNA clones were identified, sequenced and pharmacologically characterized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular cloning and functional characterization of the human alpha 2 adrenergic (AR) receptor.
the development of alpha1-adrenergic receptor subtype selective antagonists for the treatment of hypertension and other cardiovascular disorders.
the development of alpha1 adrenoceptor antagonists.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

human and bovine (and probably rat) alpha 1c receptors are not identical, but are closely similar, whereas human and hamster (and probably rat and bovine) alpha 1b receptors are identical, and that human and rat (and probably bovine) alpha1d receptors are identical.
human alpha 1AARs have the same properties as their counterparts in rat, bovine, and hamster.
the alpha 1A adrenergic subtype has a high affinity for prazosin, and that this subtype is responsible for the alpha 1-mediated vasoconstriction of the pial vessels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the human alpha 2A and alpha 2C AR subtypes have similar properties to their bovine counterparts, the human alpha 3 AR has properties similar to the rat and hamster homolog, and the human alpha 4 AR has properties similar the rat homolog.
human alpha 1 ARs are very similar in structure, function and pharmacology to those of other species, with only a few species-specific differences.

human and rat alpha 2AR subtypes are highly homologous, whereas human and rat alpha1AR subtypes are more similar to each other than to other species homologs, but all three subtypes are more homologous to their respective species than to each other.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the alpha 1A and alpha 1D subtypes of the adrenergic alpha-1 receptor can be differentiated pharmacologically.
the pharmacological profiles of the human alpha1 adrenergiceptors (a1a, a1b and a1c) are very similar to those reported for their rat and bovine counterparts.

the human alpha 2A adrenergic (alpha 2A-AR) subtype, which is the most abundant of the alpha 2AR subtypes in the brain, has a higher affinity for the agonists noradrenaline (NE) and adrenaline than do the alpha 2B and alpha 2C subtypes.
